2026-06-19 measure-twice (NO code written — bounded before implementing). git cache-off opcode profile (11.3M ops): #1 bigram MAKE_THUNK→SET_LOCAL 7.04% (85% of all MAKE_THUNKs store-to-local), anchors most top trigrams → looked like the prime OP_MAKE_THUNK_SET_LOCAL fusion candidate. BUT bounded the WHOLE fusion lever via the existing gated stack-op fusions: git cache-off fuse-ON (SET_LOCAL_KEEP+GET_LOCAL2 default) 4.77s vs fuse-OFF (NIX_V3_NO_FUSE_SETGET=1) 4.66s — fusion-OFF same-or-FASTER (within ±0.1-0.2s noise) = the entire existing fusion suite is ≤2.3% (likely ~0) on git, so one more pairwise fusion is FAR below 3%. ROOT: MAKE_THUNK is a heap ALLOCATION not a dispatch — fusing make+store removes a dispatch+push/pop but NOT the alloc (the real cost). git's "body-dispatch ceiling" is THUNK-ALLOCATION-bound + heavy-opcode-bound (CALL_PRIMOP/ATTRS_SELECT_DYN/STR_CONCAT doing real work), NOT stack-op-dispatch-bound. The only remaining git CPU lever is ALLOCATING FEWER THUNKS (strictness/demand analysis — don't thunk a binding immediately forced) = large/risky/multi-week, NOT a peephole. Opcode counts (git): GET_UPVALUE 14.5%, SET_LOCAL 11.8%, GET_LOCAL+GET_LOCAL2 17.4%, MAKE_THUNK 8.3%, RETURN 7.1%, BRANCH_FALSE 4.5% — already heavily fused (GET_LOCAL2/SET_LOCAL_KEEP/GET_UPVALUE_REC_BINDING_SLOT/TAIL_CALL_N/CALL_N exist).
